questions.prompt: What does 'visceral' convey about the author's response to Rothko's paintings?
questions.promptZh: visceral 怎样形容作者对 Rothko 画作的反应？
options: A response limited to calculating a purchase price.
A detached judgement with no felt impact.
A factual claim that he physically enters the canvas.
An immediate, deeply felt experience rather than merely an abstract judgement.
optionsZh: 仅计算买价的反应。
毫无感受影响的超然判断。
身体实际进入画布的事实主张。
直接而切身强烈的体验，不只是抽象判断。
analyses: A 没有购买价格或投资评价。
B unique, visceral 与后句 calming、absorbing、moving 不符冷漠。
C looking at 不表示进入画布。
D visceral 指切身感受；always 在这里属作者个人报告，不保证每人同效，也不确立背景知识的必然因果。

vocabulary.meaning: 切身强烈的；出于直觉和深层感受的
vocabulary.context: 形容看画体验，不是医学上内脏的诊断。
vocabulary.example: The final scene produced a visceral response in the viewer.

questions.evidenceQuote: For me, arts and sports provide rare moments to escape the endless chatter of everyday life. Looking at Mark Rothko’s No. 13 (White, Red on Yellow) and his other color field paintings is always a unique, visceral experience. The simple color and fuzzy lines are calming, absorbing, even moving, maybe because I know Rothko was depressed and ultimately took his own life.

questions.prompt: What action does the author say he has taken in front of the painting?
questions.promptZh: 作者说自己曾在画作前做什么？
options: Sat in front of it on repeated visits.
Purchased it and moved it to his house.
Painted it while working in the museum.
Interviewed every visitor before allowing them to look.
optionsZh: 多次在它面前坐着。
买下并搬到家。
在博物馆工作时画出它。
先采访每个访客才允许他们看。
analyses: A I’ve sat in front of...many times 是亲身回顾，引用完整跨候选句以免 No. 缩写误断。
B 无购买或搬走画作。
C 作者在观看，不是声称自己创作。
D 无访客访问控制；many times 不是可凭空给出的精确次数。

vocabulary.context: 现在完成时回顾多次观看经历，不表示此刻每个时刻都在那里。
vocabulary.example: I've sat beside the window many times to sketch the view.

questions.evidenceQuote: Or maybe it has nothing to do with this background knowledge. I’ve sat in front of No. 13 in the Metropolitan Museum of Art many times. It draws me in and I forget about everything else.

questions.prompt: Where does the author locate these repeated visits to No. 13?
questions.promptZh: 作者把反复观看 No. 13 的经历定位在哪里？
options: At his own home in Japan.
Inside Darlington Hall during wartime.
In the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
In the Park family's house in Parasite.
optionsZh: 日本自己家中。
战时 Darlington 庄园内。
Metropolitan Museum of Art。
Parasite 中 Park 家。
analyses: A 未说家中或日本。
B 庄园属小说阅读场景，不是此处看画地点。
C in the Metropolitan Museum of Art 明确地点，many times 不改成某年某日。
D 不能跨电影错配；这是书中作者观看经历，不是网站当前展览信息。

vocabulary.context: 指观看画作时的位置，不是拥有画作或正在画中。
vocabulary.example: The visitors paused in front of the painting.
collocations: in the Metropolitan Museum of Art

questions.evidenceQuote: Or maybe it has nothing to do with this background knowledge. I’ve sat in front of No. 13 in the Metropolitan Museum of Art many times. It draws me in and I forget about everything else.

questions.prompt: What does 'It draws me in' describe in the author's account?
questions.promptZh: It draws me in 在作者叙述中描写什么？
options: The painting is physically sketching the author.
The work absorbs his attention so strongly that other concerns fade.
The museum requires him to submit a drawing.
He remembers every other task more clearly while avoiding the painting.
optionsZh: 画作正在实际画作者。
作品强烈吸引注意，使其他事淡出。
博物馆要求他提交一幅画。
他避开画作时更清楚记得其他所有任务。
analyses: A draws...in 是吸引进入体验，不是 draw 作画。
B and I forget about everything else 展开被吸引的结果，属沉浸描述。
C 没有提交作品要求。
D 与 forget、draws me in 双双相反；不是对记忆功能的医学结论。

vocabulary.meaning: 把我吸引进去；使我投入
vocabulary.context: draw in 的熟词偏义，指注意被作品吸引，不是铅笔绘制或身体进入。
vocabulary.example: The opening paragraph draws the reader in immediately.

questions.evidenceQuote: Or maybe it has nothing to do with this background knowledge. I’ve sat in front of No. 13 in the Metropolitan Museum of Art many times. It draws me in and I forget about everything else.

questions.prompt: What is Berlyne said to have done in his 1971 book?
questions.promptZh: 书中说 Berlyne 在 1971 年著作中做了什么？
options: Written the abstract poem The Life of Haifisch.
Summarised a series of experiments on aesthetic judgement.
Claimed that no experiments on aesthetics had ever been attempted.
Conducted the later childhood-reading survey with the author.
optionsZh: 创作抽象诗 The Life of Haifisch。
总结一系列审美判断实验。
声称此前从未有人尝试美学实验。
与本书作者实施后来的童年阅读调查。
analyses: A 诗作者在后面另归 Scott MacLeod。
B 1971、书名与 summarized a series of experiments 对应，不误作只一项新实验。
C series of experiments 排除从无实验的改写。
D 将后面的作者团队调查错配给 Berlyne。

vocabulary.context: 说明书中汇总一系列实验，不等于该书只报告单个实验。
vocabulary.example: The chapter summarized several studies of attention.

questions.evidenceQuote: In his 1971 book, Aesthetics and Psychobiology, Daniel Berlyne summarized a series of experiments on aesthetic judgments. His major finding was that there are different, optimal levels of complexity for pleasantness and interestingness. Simple geometric figures are typically perceived to be more pleasant than complex ones, whereas complex ones are typically perceived to be more interesting than simple ones.

questions.prompt: Which pattern does the passage describe for simple and complex figures?
questions.promptZh: 片段描述简单与复杂图形的哪种模式？
options: Simple figures are typically more interesting and less pleasant.
Complexity raises pleasantness and interestingness to identical levels.
Simple figures are always preferred on every rating by every participant.
Simple figures tend to be more pleasant, whereas complex ones tend to be more interesting.
optionsZh: 简单图通常更有趣且更不愉悦。
复杂性使两种评分升到相同程度。
每个参与者在每项评分永远都偏好简单图。
简单图通常更愉悦，复杂图通常更有趣。
analyses: A 把两个评价方向颠倒。
B passage 区分两维最佳复杂程度，不说同一水平。
C typically 不是 always，且趣味方向相反。
D whereas 明示愉悦与有趣可走不同方向，不把群体倾向改成人人定律。

vocabulary.context: 将不同评分维度并列比较，不表示后者是前者的原因。
vocabulary.example: The first design was simpler, whereas the second was more unusual.

questions.evidenceQuote: In his 1971 book, Aesthetics and Psychobiology, Daniel Berlyne summarized a series of experiments on aesthetic judgments. His major finding was that there are different, optimal levels of complexity for pleasantness and interestingness. Simple geometric figures are typically perceived to be more pleasant than complex ones, whereas complex ones are typically perceived to be more interesting than simple ones.

questions.prompt: What combinations were represented among the geometric figures?
questions.promptZh: 几何图形包含哪些组合？
options: Simple or complex figures, each with symmetrical and asymmetrical versions.
Only simple and symmetrical figures, repeated without variation.
Only complex figures, with no comparison involving symmetry.
Four groups distinguished solely by their colour and price.
optionsZh: 简单或复杂各分别有对称与不对称版本。
只有简单对称图，无变化重复。
只有复杂图，不比较对称性。
四组只按颜色与价格区分。
analyses: A 两因素的四种组合原文逐项列出。
B 漏掉其余三种。
C 同时漏掉简单条件和对称条件。
D 操纵的是 symmetry 和 number of elements，不是颜色价钱；不据此添加未述随机分派程序。

vocabulary.context: 与复杂性是不同维度，简单也可不对称，复杂也可对称。
vocabulary.example: The design was simple but asymmetrical.

questions.evidenceQuote: In one experiment, Berlyne manipulated two factors of geometric figures: the first was symmetry (i.e., how symmetrical and homogeneous elements were), and the other was the number of elements (i.e., one to five elements vs. numerous elements). Some figures were simple and symmetrical, some were simple and asymmetrical, some were complex and symmetrical, and the others were complex and asymmetrical. Participants rated the simple and symmetrical figures to be the most pleasant, followed by complex and symmetrical, simple and asymmetrical, and complex and asymmetrical. Symmetry was key to pleasantness.

questions.prompt: Which figure type came second in the reported pleasantness ranking?
questions.promptZh: 所报愉悦评分排序中，哪种图排第二？
options: Simple and asymmetrical.
Complex and asymmetrical.
Complex and symmetrical.
Simple and symmetrical.
optionsZh: 简单不对称。
复杂不对称。
复杂对称。
简单对称。
analyses: A 列表第三，不是第二。
B 排第四。
C 最愉悦 simple and symmetrical 后接 followed by complex and symmetrical。
D 是第一；此处排序对象为 pleasant，不要挪用 interesting 的排序。

vocabulary.context: 在评级叙述中标示名次顺序，不是说参与者在空间上跟随图形。
vocabulary.example: The largest group was followed by two smaller groups.

questions.evidenceQuote: In one experiment, Berlyne manipulated two factors of geometric figures: the first was symmetry (i.e., how symmetrical and homogeneous elements were), and the other was the number of elements (i.e., one to five elements vs. numerous elements). Some figures were simple and symmetrical, some were simple and asymmetrical, some were complex and symmetrical, and the others were complex and asymmetrical. Participants rated the simple and symmetrical figures to be the most pleasant, followed by complex and symmetrical, simple and asymmetrical, and complex and asymmetrical. Symmetry was key to pleasantness.

questions.prompt: What does 'Symmetry was key to pleasantness' identify?
questions.promptZh: Symmetry was key to pleasantness 指出什么？
options: Symmetry was the only factor ever measured in any art study.
Symmetry was important to pleasantness in this reported comparison.
Symmetry made the same figures the most interesting as well.
Every asymmetric artwork must be rejected by every viewer.
optionsZh: 对称是任何美学研究唯一测量因素。
在所报比较中，对称性对愉悦很重要。
对称也使同样图形最有趣。
每位观众都必须排斥每件不对称作品。
analyses: A 实验还操纵元素数量，不能加 only 或所有研究。
B key 说明该评价维度的重要因素，保留当前实验范围。
C 后文简单对称最无趣，两维不可混同。
D 没有对全部艺术与观众的命令或全称拒绝。

vocabulary.context: 图形两侧或元素关系的特征；与 simple/complex 和有趣/愉悦各需区分。
vocabulary.example: Symmetry gave the pattern a balanced appearance.

questions.evidenceQuote: In one experiment, Berlyne manipulated two factors of geometric figures: the first was symmetry (i.e., how symmetrical and homogeneous elements were), and the other was the number of elements (i.e., one to five elements vs. numerous elements). Some figures were simple and symmetrical, some were simple and asymmetrical, some were complex and symmetrical, and the others were complex and asymmetrical. Participants rated the simple and symmetrical figures to be the most pleasant, followed by complex and symmetrical, simple and asymmetrical, and complex and asymmetrical. Symmetry was key to pleasantness.

questions.prompt: What opposite effects are reported for complexity and asymmetry?
questions.promptZh: 复杂性与不对称被报告有哪组相反效果？
options: They made both ratings disappear from the task.
They decreased interestingness but increased pleasantness.
They guaranteed that all viewers disliked all complex art.
They increased interestingness while reducing pleasantness in this comparison.
optionsZh: 使任务中两类评分消失。
降低趣味而提高愉悦。
保证所有观众不喜欢一切复杂艺术。
在此比较中提高趣味，却降低愉悦。
analyses: A 两种评分均被报告，非消失。
B 将两方向同时颠倒。
C 当前图形评级不能扩大到所有观众与艺术，也不把 interesting 当 dislike。
D added interestingness 与 detracted from pleasantness 对照，明确两维分开。

vocabulary.context: 与 added 对照，指愉悦程度下降，不是两维都下降。
vocabulary.example: The clutter detracted from the clarity of the illustration.

questions.evidenceQuote: Yet, Berlyne found that participants rated simple and symmetrical figures (rated most pleasing) to also be the least interesting. Complexity and asymmetry added interestingness, whereas they detracted from pleasantness.

questions.prompt: Which researchers are named at the start of the later painting experiment account?
questions.promptZh: 较后绘画实验介绍的开头点名哪两位研究者？
options: Paul Silvia and Samuel Turner Jr.
Daniel Berlyne and Claude Monet.
Scott MacLeod and Mark Rothko.
Erin Westgate and Nick Buttrick.
optionsZh: Paul Silvia 与 Samuel Turner Jr.。
Daniel Berlyne 与 Claude Monet。
Scott MacLeod 与 Mark Rothko。
Erin Westgate 与 Nick Buttrick。
analyses: A 两位名字在 More recently 后明确，Jr. 是姓名后缀，非句子实际终结。
B 混合此前研究者与画家。
C 是诗人与画家，不是此项研究组合。
D 属后面的作者阅读调查合作团队，不能挪来；recently 相对书中叙述，不是最新研究认证。

vocabulary.context: 这里为原书研究叙事中的相对时间，不声称当前最新研究。
vocabulary.example: More recently, the team examined a different type of task.

questions.evidenceQuote: More recently, Paul Silvia and Samuel Turner Jr. conducted an intriguing experiment on aesthetic judgments. Participants looked at thirteen classical paintings, six of which were calming, such as Dance Foyer at the Opera by Edgar Degas and The Water Lily Pond by Claude Monet. The other seven were disturbing, such as Francis Bacon’s Figure with Meat (the pope in horror surrounded by two cow carcasses) and Francisco Goya’s Saturn Devouring His Son (yes, a god eating human flesh).

questions.prompt: What was the topic of the experiment conducted by Silvia and Turner?
questions.promptZh: Silvia 与 Turner 所做实验的主题是什么？
options: Verifying the actors' biographies in The Matrix.
Measuring the price of every classical painting.
Aesthetic judgements, using participants' responses to paintings.
Testing childhood reading by assigning children lifelong genres.
optionsZh: 核实 The Matrix 演员生平。
测每幅古典画价格。
通过参与者对画作反应研究审美判断。
给儿童分派终身阅读类型来测童年阅读。
analyses: A 不是电影人物生平任务。
B 看画并评分，不是价格研究。
C conducted...on aesthetic judgments 后说明十三幅画及评价，引用完整原句连接被 Jr. 误断的主语与谓语。
D 童年阅读调查在后文，且不能写成随机指定终身体裁。

vocabulary.meaning: 审美判断；对作品体验特征的评价
vocabulary.context: 此处通过画作反应研究，不是仅按市场价格判价值。
vocabulary.example: The study compared aesthetic judgments across several images.
collocations: an intriguing experiment on aesthetic judgments

questions.evidenceQuote: More recently, Paul Silvia and Samuel Turner Jr. conducted an intriguing experiment on aesthetic judgments. Participants looked at thirteen classical paintings, six of which were calming, such as Dance Foyer at the Opera by Edgar Degas and The Water Lily Pond by Claude Monet. The other seven were disturbing, such as Francis Bacon’s Figure with Meat (the pope in horror surrounded by two cow carcasses) and Francisco Goya’s Saturn Devouring His Son (yes, a god eating human flesh).

questions.prompt: What contrast is made with Monet's painting?
questions.promptZh: 与 Monet 画作作了什么对照？
options: Monet's work is described as the most grotesque of all the paintings.
All paintings are said to be equally serene with no meaningful difference.
The paintings under discussion are shocking and grotesque by comparison with Monet's serene warmth.
Monet is described as the participant rather than the painter.
optionsZh: Monet 作品被说成全部画中最怪诞。
所有画都同样宁静、毫无区别。
所谈画相对 Monet 的宁静温暖显得震撼怪诞。
Monet 被说成参与者而非画家。
analyses: A serene,warm 修饰 Monet，不能反向归 grotesque。
B particularly in comparison 明确对照。
C 两组形容词及比较对象原文明示；当前短段不要求猜未重述的前段作品名。
D by Monet 表作者归属，不是评分参与者。

vocabulary.meaning: 怪诞的；奇异而令人不适的
vocabulary.context: 与 serene,warm 对照，不等同作者在此判定作品没有价值或无趣。
vocabulary.example: The unusual masks gave the scene a grotesque quality.

questions.evidenceQuote: These paintings are quite shocking and grotesque, particularly in comparison to the famously serene, warm painting by Monet. After looking at each painting, participants reported how interesting or uninteresting, boring or engaging, enjoyable or unenjoyable, pleasing or displeasing, comprehensible or incomprehensible, familiar or unfamiliar each painting was. Results showed that pleasantness ratings were predicted by comprehensibleness, familiarity, and simpleness. In other words, the easier to understand and simpler the paintings were, the more pleasant they were.

questions.prompt: What did participants do after looking at each painting?
questions.promptZh: 参与者每看完一幅画后做什么？
options: Reported their experience along several contrasting dimensions, including interest, pleasure, comprehension, and familiarity.
Reported objective artist identities and art-history facts rather than their impressions.
Gave only a single overall enjoyment rating, with interest and comprehension omitted.
Described one selected painting from memory before looking at it.
optionsZh: 沿多组对照维度报告体验，包括趣味、愉悦、理解与熟悉程度。
报告客观画家身份与艺术史事实，而非感受。
只给单一整体享受分，省略兴趣与理解。
观看前先凭记忆描述一幅选定画。
analyses: A how...多个对照词说明多维主观评分，不能把 interesting 与 enjoyable 合成一项。
B how...interesting、enjoyable 等是体验维度，不是事实测验。
C 列表明确含兴趣、理解等多个维度，不能合并成单一享受。
D After looking at each painting 限定每幅看完后报告，不是看前仅凭记忆一幅。

vocabulary.context: 与 boring 对照，指体验投入程度，不是这里订婚的词义。
vocabulary.example: The unfamiliar story was engaging despite its difficult structure.

questions.evidenceQuote: These paintings are quite shocking and grotesque, particularly in comparison to the famously serene, warm painting by Monet. After looking at each painting, participants reported how interesting or uninteresting, boring or engaging, enjoyable or unenjoyable, pleasing or displeasing, comprehensible or incomprehensible, familiar or unfamiliar each painting was. Results showed that pleasantness ratings were predicted by comprehensibleness, familiarity, and simpleness. In other words, the easier to understand and simpler the paintings were, the more pleasant they were.

questions.prompt: What relationship is restated by 'In other words'?
questions.promptZh: In other words 重述哪种关系？
options: Less comprehensible and more complicated paintings received higher pleasantness ratings.
All paintings were rated equally pleasant, regardless of their features.
The passage establishes that familiarity is irrelevant to every viewer.
Easier-to-understand and simpler paintings were rated as more pleasant in the reported results.
optionsZh: 越难懂越复杂的画，愉悦评分越高。
所有画不论特征都同样愉悦。
确立熟悉性与每个观众都无关。
所报结果中，越易懂、越简单的画愉悦评分越高。
analyses: A 两个比较方向反了。
B the...the... 表随特征变化的关系，不是全同。
C 前句熟悉性也预测 pleasantness，不能说无关。
D 重述 ease、simplicity 与 pleasantness 的对应；predicted by 不自动证明每个特征对所有人有独立确定因果。

vocabulary.context: 重述前句结果，不是引入新的样本或全新实验。
vocabulary.example: The task required retention; in other words, the details had to stay in memory.

questions.evidenceQuote: These paintings are quite shocking and grotesque, particularly in comparison to the famously serene, warm painting by Monet. After looking at each painting, participants reported how interesting or uninteresting, boring or engaging, enjoyable or unenjoyable, pleasing or displeasing, comprehensible or incomprehensible, familiar or unfamiliar each painting was. Results showed that pleasantness ratings were predicted by comprehensibleness, familiarity, and simpleness. In other words, the easier to understand and simpler the paintings were, the more pleasant they were.

questions.prompt: Which features predicted interestingness ratings in this account?
questions.promptZh: 此处哪些特征预测趣味评分？
options: Comprehensibleness and familiarity, exactly as for pleasantness.
Disturbingness and unpleasantness.
Symmetry and a small number of geometric elements.
Familiarity alone, with no contribution from unpleasantness.
optionsZh: 与愉悦完全相同的可理解性和熟悉性。
扰人程度与不愉悦程度。
对称性与少量几何元素。
仅熟悉性，不愉悦没有贡献。
analyses: A 将前面愉悦的预测特征直接移给趣味，忽略 In contrast。
B 原句明确两项 predictors，不能换成 pleasantness 的变量。
C 对称及元素数属前面几何图操纵，不能替代此项画作评分结果。
D 原文明确 unpleasantness，不能删除；统计预测不升级为必然因果。

vocabulary.meaning: 由……在统计上预测；与所述评分相关
vocabulary.context: 此处描述评价指标之间的结果，不单凭这词认定独立因果或未来人人必然反应。
vocabulary.example: In the analysis, interest ratings were predicted by novelty.

questions.evidenceQuote: In contrast, interestingness ratings were predicted by disturbingness and unpleasantness. That is, the more disturbing and unpleasant they were, the more interesting the paintings were.

questions.prompt: What question did Silvia explore in the other experiment introduced here?
questions.promptZh: 这里介绍的另一项实验探索什么？
options: The role of comprehension in responding to art.
Whether the same painting could be sold at thirteen prices.
Whether childhood reading had already been randomly assigned.
The actual historical biography of Mr. Stevens.
optionsZh: 理解在艺术反应中的作用。
同一画能否按十三个价格售出。
童年阅读是否已被随机分派。
Stevens 的真实历史生平。
analyses: A role of comprehension 明确研究焦点，后面诗与背景资料说明实施。
B thirteen 属前项画作数，不是价格条件。
C 未说对童年长期阅读随机分派。
D 不是小说角色史实核验；与前绘画评分区分为 another experiment。

vocabulary.meaning: 理解；理解所读内容的能力或程度
vocabulary.context: 在此为能否读懂作品，不是简单喜欢、记住或熟悉三个概念的同义词。
vocabulary.example: Background information improved comprehension of the poem.

questions.evidenceQuote: In another experiment, Silvia explored the role of comprehension. For instance, participants were asked to read Scott MacLeod’s famously abstract poem The Life of Haifisch. Those who were not provided with any background information could not understand it and did not find it interesting. In contrast, the other participants who read the same poem but with more background information, such as its title and the explanation that Haifisch means “shark” in German, found it more comprehensible and far more interesting.

questions.prompt: What material were participants asked to read in the example?
questions.promptZh: 例子中，参与者被要求读什么材料？
options: A technical guide written by Claude Monet.
The novel The Remains of the Day by Paul Silvia.
Scott MacLeod's abstract poem The Life of Haifisch.
A new biography of the participants themselves.
optionsZh: Claude Monet 写的技术指南。
Paul Silvia 写的 The Remains of the Day。
Scott MacLeod 的抽象诗 The Life of Haifisch。
参与者自己的新传记。
analyses: A Monet 是前面画家，不是此处作者。
B 书名、作者与媒介均错配。
C 名字、作品名与 abstract poem 在本句准确对应。
D 没有参与者自传任务；不从诗名直接添加未述完整诗内容。

vocabulary.meaning: 抽象的；不易按具体叙事直读的
vocabulary.context: 这里形容诗的表达，不是名词摘要或自动等于无意义。
vocabulary.example: The abstract poem became clearer after a brief introduction.

questions.evidenceQuote: In another experiment, Silvia explored the role of comprehension. For instance, participants were asked to read Scott MacLeod’s famously abstract poem The Life of Haifisch. Those who were not provided with any background information could not understand it and did not find it interesting. In contrast, the other participants who read the same poem but with more background information, such as its title and the explanation that Haifisch means “shark” in German, found it more comprehensible and far more interesting.

questions.prompt: How did the participants without background information respond to the poem?
questions.promptZh: 没有背景资料的参与者对诗怎样反应？
options: They understood it fully and found it the most interesting text possible.
They reported the same comprehension advantage as the informed group.
They were given the German meaning of Haifisch before reading.
They could not understand it and did not find it interesting in this reported comparison.
optionsZh: 完全理解，并认为它是最有趣的文本。
报告与获资料组相同的理解优势。
阅读前已获 Haifisch 的德语释义。
在所述比较中无法理解，也不觉得有趣。
analyses: A 与两项否定都反。
B In contrast 后另一组更易懂更有趣，并非同样优势。
C shark 释义给另一组，不能挪给无背景组。
D not provided、could not understand、did not find interesting 三项对应，不推广成所有难诗都永远不可欣赏。

vocabulary.meaning: 背景信息；帮助理解作品的资料
vocabulary.context: 此实验如标题和词义提示，不是改变诗文本或参与者的童年。
vocabulary.example: A little background information helped readers follow the unusual poem.
collocations: not provided with any background information
the same poem but with more background information

questions.evidenceQuote: In another experiment, Silvia explored the role of comprehension. For instance, participants were asked to read Scott MacLeod’s famously abstract poem The Life of Haifisch. Those who were not provided with any background information could not understand it and did not find it interesting. In contrast, the other participants who read the same poem but with more background information, such as its title and the explanation that Haifisch means “shark” in German, found it more comprehensible and far more interesting.

questions.prompt: What does 'an intricate line' mean in this short passage?
questions.promptZh: 短段里的 an intricate line 是什么意思？
options: A line physically drawn on a painting to hide its title.
A subtle boundary concerning how comprehensible art needs to be for appreciation.
A fixed queue of participants waiting outside the museum.
An instruction that complete incomprehensibility is necessary for appreciation.
optionsZh: 画上实际画来遮标题的线。
关于艺术至少须多可理解才能欣赏的微妙界线。
博物馆外参与者固定队列。
认为欣赏必须完全无法理解的要求。
analyses: A 下一句谈欣赏条件，不是画面线条。
B intricate 描写关系微妙，must be at least minimally comprehensible 给界线内容。
C line 在此不是排队。
D minimally comprehensible 是至少最低限度能懂，不能反成完全难懂。

vocabulary.context: 这里形容概念界线，并非统计上已给出固定分数阈值。
vocabulary.example: The debate revealed an intricate relationship between difficulty and interest.

questions.evidenceQuote: There is an intricate line. For art to be appreciated, it must be at least minimally comprehensible.

questions.prompt: What did the author do with Westgate and Buttrick at the University of Virginia?
questions.promptZh: 作者在 University of Virginia 与 Westgate、Buttrick 一起做什么？
options: Read the existing research literature on experimental aesthetics.
Wrote the abstract poem used in Silvia's experiment.
Managed Darlington Hall during the war.
Assigned each participant a lifelong profession in art.
optionsZh: 阅读已有实验美学研究文献。
创作 Silvia 实验所用抽象诗。
在战争中管理 Darlington 庄园。
给每个参与者分派终身艺术职业。
analyses: A with whom I read the existing literature...such as Paul Silvia’s 对应，literature 在这里是学术文献。
B 诗已归 Scott MacLeod，不能当本组创作。
C 混入小说人物经历。
D 没有终身岗位分派；原文交代两位当时学生的合作背景，不声称其当前身份仍相同。

vocabulary.meaning: 研究文献；某领域已有学术著述
vocabulary.context: 在 existing literature on experimental aesthetics 中不是专指文学小说，与下一句 books 研究对象区分。
vocabulary.example: The team reviewed the literature before designing the survey.
collocations: the existing literature on experimental aesthetics

questions.evidenceQuote: While at the University of Virginia, I had the chance to work with two students, Erin Westgate and Nick Buttrick, with whom I read the existing literature on experimental aesthetics such as Paul Silvia’s. We wondered if reading all kinds of books early on in life helped readers appreciate more complexity and lead an intellectually rich life. So we asked over 5,000 people about their reading habits during childhood, their current cognitive styles, and their perceived levels of psychological richness.

questions.prompt: What status does 'We wondered if' give the proposed link about early reading?
questions.promptZh: We wondered if 使关于早期阅读的联系处于什么状态？
options: It is a completed causal proof before data are collected.
It records each participant's actual childhood reading choice as random assignment.
It introduces a research question that the later survey was intended to explore.
It says every kind of book has already been proved equally beneficial.
optionsZh: 收集资料前已完成因果证明。
把每个人童年阅读选择记录为随机分派。
提出后来调查拟探索的研究问题。
说所有体裁已证明同样有益。
analyses: A wondered if 是待探问题，不是已证结果。
B 后面 asked people about childhood habits，是回顾调查而非分派童年。
C 接 So we asked over 5,000 people，清楚呈现提问与调查顺序。
D all kinds 是想探索的范围，不是证实每体裁同效；不从措辞 helped 擅定因果已成立。

vocabulary.meaning: 想知道是否；对某可能联系提出疑问
vocabulary.context: 标示研究问题，区别后文结果与作者原先假设。
vocabulary.example: They wondered if the activity was related to later interests.

questions.evidenceQuote: While at the University of Virginia, I had the chance to work with two students, Erin Westgate and Nick Buttrick, with whom I read the existing literature on experimental aesthetics such as Paul Silvia’s. We wondered if reading all kinds of books early on in life helped readers appreciate more complexity and lead an intellectually rich life. So we asked over 5,000 people about their reading habits during childhood, their current cognitive styles, and their perceived levels of psychological richness.

questions.prompt: How should 'We assumed that reading ... would be associated with' be read?
questions.promptZh: We assumed that reading...would be associated with 应怎样理解？
options: As an already established result that the researchers are simply repeating.
As final proof that every genre independently causes cognitive flexibility.
As a report that the findings were exactly as simple as expected.
As an initial expectation of an association, followed by the admission that results were more intricate.
optionsZh: 作为研究者仅仅复述的既定结果。
作为每种体裁独立导致认知灵活的最终证明。
作为结果正如预期简单的报告。
作为最初对相关的预期，后面承认结果更复杂。
analyses: A assumed 标记事前预期，不是已确立发现；下一句才谈结果比预期更复杂。
B assumed 不是 proved，associated with 不是必然导致。
C next sentence more intricate than anticipated 恰与简单完全一致相反。
D 保留假设与结果的时序、相关与因果的区别，不让预期代替发现。

vocabulary.context: 不是仅凭词组即证明前者造成后者，也不能删除 assumed 的预期性质。
vocabulary.example: The survey examined whether reading was associated with greater flexibility.

questions.evidenceQuote: We assumed that reading in general would be associated with a more flexible cognitive style and more psychological richness. Our findings were more intricate than we had anticipated.

questions.prompt: What comparison is made about readers who grew up reading more romance?
questions.promptZh: 对童年更多读言情的人作了什么比较？
options: They all necessarily became incapable of considering any alternative reason.
They seemed to essentialize more than those who had read less romance.
They were randomly assigned to read no other books for life.
They were shown to be more attributionally complex than every literary-fiction reader.
optionsZh: 他们全必然无法考虑任何其他原因。
他们似乎比较少读言情者更倾向本质化。
他们被随机分派终身不得读其他书。
证明他们比每个文学小说读者都更有归因复杂性。
analyses: A seemed 和 greater degree 不是全称绝对能力缺失。
B 原句比较对象、方向、程度及似乎均对应；这些是回顾调查联系。
C 无终身体裁随机分派。
D 文段方向相反，也不能将组间倾向写成每个个体的排序或确定因果。

vocabulary.meaning: 本质化；以固定简单特质概括人或事
vocabulary.context: 结合本段归因复杂性，区别考虑多种原因；不是这里把某事变重要。
vocabulary.example: The discussion warned against essentializing people with a single label.

questions.evidenceQuote: First, as predicted, individuals who grew up reading a lot of literary fiction were indeed more attributionally complex (i.e., able to think of multiple reasons why someone might behave a certain way) and led a psychologically richer life as adults than those who did not. Second, unexpectedly, those who grew up reading a lot of romance novels were significantly less attributionally complex than those who did not. These readers seemed to “essentialize” to a greater degree than those who had read less romance.

questions.prompt: What do the Joe, Jill, baseball, and opera examples illustrate?
questions.promptZh: Joe、Jill、棒球与歌剧的例子说明什么？
options: The researchers' verified moral judgements about four actual participants.
A detailed account of several competing reasons for every person's behaviour.
The simplified, fixed-label outlook used to illustrate the tendency being discussed.
A rule that every reader must dislike baseball and avoid opera.
optionsZh: 研究者对四位真实参与者已核实的道德评价。
对每个人行为多种竞争原因的详细解释。
用来说明所述倾向的简化、固定贴标签视角。
每位读者必须讨厌棒球、避开歌剧的规则。
analyses: A For instance 是示例，不是这几位真实受试者的人格认证。
B jerk、angel、bore 等固定标签展示 simplistic，非细致多因解释。
C 举例把 more simplistic view 具体化；tended 保留倾向，不能扩大全部言情读者。
D 观点例子不是作者命令或对读者偏好的真实记录，也不能当体裁导致本质化的证明。

vocabulary.meaning: 过度简单化的；忽略复杂性的
vocabulary.context: 不同于仅仅清晰或简洁，当前用固定标签说明忽略情境。
vocabulary.example: The essay rejected a simplistic explanation of the character's choice.
collocations: a more simplistic view of the world

questions.evidenceQuote: For instance, early romance readers tended to hold a more simplistic view of the world: Joe is a jerk, Jill is an angel, baseball is a bore, opera is for old people, and so on.
